title: One brings another (Avot 4:2)
hookLine: Ben Azzai: run to an easy mitzvah; one good deed draws the next
tomorrow: the person nobody picks: does Ben Azzai have a word?

cards: Apps pay you for a streak with badges, coins and confetti. Ben Azzai offers a stranger reward.
Run to an easy mitzvah, he says, and flee from a transgression, for one mitzvah brings another, and one transgression brings another. Then the odd part: the reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah.
You do a good deed, and your prize is another good deed to do.

teach.b: So why pay in the same coin? Start with the run. Ben Azzai doesn't say run to the big, heroic mitzvah.
He says the easy one, mitzvah kalah, the one that seems too small to matter. Small things are where habits start, and habits pull.
Mitzvah goreret mitzvah: a good deed drags the next one along behind it. Hold one door, and you're already someone who notices the next door.
The other direction works the same way, which is why he says flee, not walk. Now the paycheck. Sechar mitzvah, mitzvah.
Readers take it more than one way. One: the best reward for doing good is the chance to do more, because the deed is the gift. Another: the deed changes the doer, so the next one comes easier.
Either way, the pay isn't outside the deed.
And since a mitzvah is a commandment, the reward is being asked again.

how: Ben Azzai's saying is quoted when encouraging small, regular mitzvot; some Jews start with one easy practice, like a blessing before food, and let others follow.

o: a family custom handed to the next child
each good deed pulls the next one after it
a gift you pass back to whoever gave it

games.q: Ben Azzai's chain — tap the pairs.

s: Ben Azzai says to run toward the hardest mitzvah first
he says the easy one, mitzvah kalah.
he says the reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah
sechar mitzvah, mitzvah: the pay is built into the deed.
for Ben Azzai, one wrong stays a one-time thing
one transgression brings another, so flee from it.

games.q: Sunday morning, a neighbor's trash bin has blown over. it'll take a minute, and you're already late for brunch. Ben Azzai says:
o: run to it: it's easy, and one good deed draws the next.
skip it; save your energy for a bigger mitzvah later.
come back later, when there's time to do it properly.
games.why: run to an easy mitzvah. the small one is the start of the chain.

practice: Pick the smallest good thing within reach: a dish to put away, a kind reply to a message, water for a plant. Do it now, quickly, while the sit runs. Then notice whether a second small thing shows up on its own.

wordCard.voice: One brings another. Ben Azzai's mitzvah goreret mitzvah: one good deed pulls the next one behind it.

orig.note: Hebrew: a mitzvah drags along a mitzvah, Ben Azzai's chain.

carryVoice: Keep this one: one mitzvah brings another, and the pay is more of the same. Shalom, friend.
